clue.text: Albacore freshly served around northern Spanish city

indicators.note: the rearranged fish letters sit around the abbreviation for northern
a dish freshly served is newly made up, so the letters of the fish are made up afresh

explanation.surface: A tuna dish is freshly plated up somewhere in the north of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly served' rearranges ALBACORE, and 'around' wraps those letters round N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan capital is a major Spanish city on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Purchase includes round float

indicators.note: the word for purchase takes the round letter within it

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A shopper's purchase comes with a round float, perhaps for fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker floating at sea, anchored to show a channel or hazard, is a float.

clue.text: Give way concerning cure

parts.note: RE means concerning, as in a letter heading
to cure an illness is to treat it

explanation.surface: Someone yields on a point about a medical remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way, as an army does, is to fall back or withdraw.

clue.text: What has branches in Chelmsford?

indicators.note: the tree sits inside the letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which organisation has branches in an Essex town, as a bank might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests shops or banks; it means a tree's boughs. Chelmsford is the county town of Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a thing with branches, here a familiar broadleaf species.

clue.text: Thrashing one-nil where Internet games are played

indicators.note: thrashing about means flailing wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A one-nil victory in a game played over the Internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrashing' reads as a heavy defeat, which one-nil is not; it signals rearranging ONENIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Games played over the Internet are played on the web, connected to the network.

clue.text: Change round what may be shown on dial for cockpit instrument

indicators.note: the word for change goes round the dial's reading

parts.note: to change something is to alter it

parts.words: what may be shown on dial
parts.note: a clock dial shows the time

explanation.surface: A pilot adjusts the readings on a cockpit dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge in the cockpit showing an aircraft's height is a cockpit instrument.

clue.text: The way in which food's given away cold

indicators.note: the food word gives up a letter, losing the cold abbreviation

parts.note: chow is slang for food
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone describes how leftover food is handed out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative asks the manner or method of doing something, i.e. the way.

clue.text: Iliad's author is in capital of Rhodes

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: the capital, or initial, of the island's name is taken

explanation.surface: A claim that the poet of the Iliad lives in the chief city of Rhodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests the city of Rhodes; it is just the initial letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek epic poet is traditionally credited with writing the Iliad.

clue.text: Substantial work at first needing a total of four scores

indicators.note: only the first letter of work is used

parts.note: a score is twenty, so four of them total eighty

explanation.surface: An impressive piece of work needs four top marks in total.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty is heavy or important, hence substantial.

clue.text: Best man hugged by old friend

indicators.note: the man's name is held inside the old friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: The best man at a wedding gets a hug from an old friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' looks like one phrase; 'Best' is the definition and 'man' gives TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The most favourable or ideal outcome is the best one.

clue.text: Mostly lukewarm about medium speeds in music

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the letter for medium
most of the word is kept, with the last letter dropped

parts.note: tepid means lukewarm
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A lukewarm review of a musician's moderate speeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts TEPID to TEPI, which goes 'about' M.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian plural of tempo: the rates at which pieces of music are played.

clue.text: We had sound of bell spoil church piece by Mendelssohn

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd, giving these letters without the apostrophe
a bell goes ding
to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: A bell rang and spoilt the church performance of a Mendelssohn work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We had' contracts to WE'D; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's famous processional from A Midsummer Night's Dream is played as couples leave the church.

clue.text: Dish one street that's corrupt

parts.note: taken as written; that the three words also run on as one string is a coincidence, as each is clued in turn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant on one particular street is rotten to the core.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrupt person is untrustworthy and deceitful, lacking honesty.

clue.text: Really dislike half of side before cricket international

indicators.note: the second half of the word side is taken

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A player who loathes half his team before a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a top-level international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or abhor something is to dislike it intensely.

clue.text: Undertake bet for titled widow

parts.note: to do a task is to undertake it
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to place a bet on an aristocratic widow.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow holding a title or property from her late husband, such as a dowager duchess.

clue.text: Difficult adhesive

definitions.meaning: gluey, tending to stick to things

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are ordinary: tacky to the touch, and awkward to deal with.

clue.text: Enclose penalty payment after swindle

indicators.note: the penalty payment comes after the swindle in the answer

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a fine is a payment imposed as a penalty

explanation.surface: A fraudster is fined after a swindle and locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to shut in or restrict, so to enclose within limits.

clue.text: For instance, topless dress is way out

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example

indicators.note: the dress loses its top letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A topless dress, for example, is a bit outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' looks like slang for outlandish; it means an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit or means of leaving a place is a way out.

clue.text: Now grim anger is all over the place promoting conflict

indicators.note: letters all over the place are scattered and disordered

explanation.surface: Grim anger is now spreading everywhere and stirring up war.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring up war or hostility, as a hawkish politician does, is promoting conflict.

clue.text: Christmas bird takes a lot of covering

indicators.note: most of the word is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: robing is dressing or covering in robes

explanation.surface: A bird for Christmas needs plenty of wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The red-breasted robin is a traditional British Christmas-card bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted songbird is a familiar emblem on British Christmas cards.

clue.text: Put nitrogen in to check gas exhaust

indicators.note: putting something in places one piece inside another
nitrogen goes inside the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Instructions to add nitrogen to test a gas exhaust system.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or outlet through which gas or smoke escapes is a gas exhaust.

clue.text: Part of roof beginning to break in high wind

indicators.note: the initial goes inside the strong wind

parts.note: a gale is a high wind

indicators.note: only the first letter of break is taken

explanation.surface: A high wind starts to damage part of the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular end wall beneath a pitched roof is a part of the roof.

clue.text: Interlink European night train initially with Bordeaux?

indicators.note: the first letters of the three words are taken

parts.note: Bordeaux is a French wine, an example signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: A traveller on a European night train with a glass of Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist together or interweave things is to interlink them.

clue.text: Side's lost minutes in afternoon break

indicators.note: the side's word has lost a letter

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket side has lost minutes during the afternoon interval.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the afternoon interval is called tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A break in the afternoon for a cuppa and cake, also the cricket interval.

clue.text: Manage a score at cricket

definitions.meaning: a single point scored by batsmen running between wickets

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to operate or direct, and the unit of scoring in cricket.

clue.text: Will meant to be changed during trial

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: the letters of meant are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A will is meant to be altered during a court trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a verb; it is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document disposing of property after death is one's last will.
